task: It's the end of the daily stand-up. The scrum master asks if there's anything else. You have one short update. Take your turn.
say: Okay, anything else before we wrap up?
zh: 每日站会快结束了，Scrum Master 问还有没有别的事。你有一个简短的更新。抓住机会说出来。对方说：好，结束前还有别的事吗？
example: Yeah, just one quick thing from me. The test environment will be down tomorrow morning for patching.

task: Your team leader asks for thoughts on the new ticket process. You want to add an idea. Ask to add something, then say it.
say: Does anyone have any thoughts on the new ticket process?
zh: 组长问大家对新的工单流程有什么想法。你想补充一个意见。先说想补充，再说出来。对方说：大家对新的工单流程有什么想法吗？
example: Can I add something? Overall it's working well, but the categories are a bit confusing for new staff.

task: In a client workshop, your colleague Sarah has just explained the nightly backups. Build on her point with one extra detail.
say: So that's how the nightly backups will work.
zh: 在客户研讨会上，同事 Sarah 刚讲完每晚备份的方案。接着她的话补充一个细节。对方说：这就是每晚备份的工作方式。
example: Just to add to what Sarah said, we'll also keep a copy in a second region, so you're covered if one region goes down.

task: The meeting chair notices you haven't spoken yet and asks you directly. Give a short opinion and one point.
say: Raj, you've been quiet. Anything to add?
zh: 主持人注意到你还没发言，直接点名问你。简单表个态，再说一个观点。对方说：Raj，你一直没说话。有什么要补充的吗？
example: Yeah, just one small thing. I'm happy with the plan, but we should let the service desk know before we go live.

task: In a team meeting, someone asks a question that you know the answer to. Jump in and answer it.
say: Does anyone know if the firewall change went in last night?
zh: 团队会议上有人提了一个问题，你知道答案。主动接话回答。对方说：有人知道昨晚防火墙变更做了没有吗？
example: Yep, I can answer that. It went in at about nine last night, and everything looks fine this morning.

task: At the end of a product demo, the presenter asks for questions. You have one. Ask it naturally.
say: Any questions so far?
zh: 产品演示结束时，演讲人问大家有没有问题。你有一个问题，自然地提出来。对方说：到目前为止有什么问题吗？
example: Yes, I've got one. Will users need to sign in again after the update?

task: A client is talking about the migration, but they've got one fact wrong. Interrupt politely and correct it.
say: And since everything's already in Azure, the migration should be pretty quick.
zh: 客户在谈迁移，但有一个事实说错了。礼貌地打断并纠正。对方说：既然所有东西都已经在 Azure 上了，迁移应该挺快的。
example: Sorry to interrupt, but just a quick correction. The finance app is still on-prem, so that part will take a bit longer.

task: In sprint planning, people are talking fast and filling the sprint. You see a problem. Jump in before they finish.
say: So we'll put the login bug and the report changes into this sprint, and then—
zh: 迭代计划会上大家说得很快，正在往迭代里塞任务。你发现一个问题。趁他们还没说完插话。对方说：那我们把登录的 bug 和报表修改放进这个迭代，然后——
example: Can I just jump in here? The report changes depend on the API work, so I don't think they'll fit this sprint.

task: Earlier, the meeting moved on before you finished talking about licence costs. Now the chair asks for any other business. Come back to your point.
say: Right, is there anything else?
zh: 刚才你还没讲完许可证费用的事，会议就转到别的话题了。现在主持人问还有没有其他事项。把话题拉回你的观点。对方说：好，还有别的吗？
example: Yes, I'd like to come back to the licence costs. I don't think we really finished that discussion.

task: You were explaining a problem when Tom cut in with his own idea. He has stopped talking. Accept his point and take the floor back.
say: Yeah, but I think the real issue is the network.
zh: 你在解释一个问题时，Tom 插进来说了他的想法。他说完了。先认可他，再把发言权拿回来。对方说：对，但我觉得真正的问题是网络。
example: Sure, that could be part of it. But if I could just finish my point, the logs also show the database timing out.

task: In a design review, Aroha suggests a new service. You like the idea. Agree and build on it.
say: I think we should put Front Door in front of the web apps.
zh: 设计评审会上，Aroha 建议加一个新服务。你喜欢这个主意。表示同意，并在此基础上补充。对方说：我觉得应该在 Web 应用前面加上 Front Door。
example: Yeah, I like that. Building on that, we could turn on the web application firewall at the same time and get some extra protection.

task: At a steering meeting, your manager says the project is on track. You know about a risk. Add it politely without contradicting her.
say: So overall, the project is green and on track.
zh: 指导委员会会议上，经理说项目进展顺利。你知道一个风险。礼貌地补充，不要直接反驳她。对方说：总的来说，项目是绿灯，按计划进行中。
example: Could I just add one thing there? We're green for now, but the vendor still hasn't confirmed their delivery date, so that's a risk to watch.

task: The discussion was fast and you couldn't find a gap. Finally the chair notices and asks you. Say you've been trying to get in, then make your point.
say: Raj, did you want to say something?
zh: 讨论太快，你一直找不到插话的机会。终于主持人注意到了你。说你一直想发言，然后说出观点。对方说：Raj，你是不是想说什么？
example: Yes, thanks. I've been trying to get a word in. I think this plan is missing time for user testing.

task: A colleague says the team needs better documentation. Agree and suggest one practical step.
say: We really need to get better at documenting our changes.
zh: 同事说团队需要把文档做得更好。表示同意，再提一个具体可行的办法。对方说：我们真的要把变更记录做好。
example: Totally agree. Maybe we could add a documentation step to the change template, so it's harder to skip.

task: Tom is answering a client's question for you, but he gets a detail wrong. Jump in gently and give the correct status.
say: Raj set up the VPN last week, so that's all done.
zh: Tom 在替你回答客户的问题，但说错了一个细节。温和地插话，说明真实进度。对方说：Raj 上周已经把 VPN 配好了，那部分全部完成了。
example: Just to jump in there, the VPN is set up, but we're still waiting for your team to test it. So it's nearly done.

task: On an incident call, people are about to try the wrong fix. You've just found the real cause. Interrupt firmly but politely.
say: Let's restart the app service again and see if that helps.
zh: 在故障处理电话会上，大家准备试一个错误的办法。你刚找到真正的原因。坚定而礼貌地打断。对方说：我们再重启一次应用服务看看有没有用。
example: Sorry, can I stop you there? I've just checked, and the certificate expired an hour ago. Restarting won't fix it.

task: Tom has cut you off twice, and now he wants to move to the next item. Stop him politely and finish your point.
say: Okay, so moving on to the next item—
zh: Tom 已经打断你两次了，现在他又要进入下一项。礼貌地拦住他，把你的观点说完。对方说：好，那我们进入下一项——
example: Sorry, Tom, before we move on, I didn't quite get to finish my point about the backups. It'll only take a minute.

task: In a client workshop, the client's IT manager has been talking for a while. You want to add a different view without sounding rude.
say: And that's why we want everything in one subscription.
zh: 客户研讨会上，客户的 IT 经理讲了很久。你想提出不同角度，但不要显得没礼貌。对方说：这就是为什么我们想把所有东西放在一个订阅里。
example: That makes sense for keeping things simple. Can I add a slightly different angle? Separate subscriptions for production and test would actually make your billing much clearer.

task: The meeting has drifted off-topic and there are only ten minutes left. Bring everyone back to the main item.
say: And don't get me started on the old intranet.
zh: 会议跑题了，只剩十分钟。把大家拉回到主要议题。对方说：老内网的事就别提了，一说就停不下来。
example: Ha, that's a whole other meeting! Can I bring us back to the cutover plan? We've only got ten minutes and still need to agree on a date.

task: Earlier, your quiet colleague Mei made a good point about training, but nobody picked it up. Before the meeting moves on, bring it back and support her.
say: Okay, let's move on to the budget.
zh: 刚才不爱说话的同事 Mei 提了一个关于培训的好建议，但没人接。在会议继续之前，把这个话题拉回来并支持她。对方说：好，我们接下来讲预算。
example: Before we do, I'd like to go back to what Mei said earlier about user training. I think she's right, and it should be in the plan.

task: You're explaining an architecture in a design review, and Tom keeps interrupting with questions. Answer briefly and keep the floor.
say: But what about the cost of all that?
zh: 你在设计评审会上讲架构，Tom 不断插嘴提问。简短回应，同时继续掌握发言权。对方说：那这些的成本怎么算？
example: Good question, and I'll get to cost in a sec. Let me just finish the architecture bit first, then I'll go through the numbers.

task: In a sprint review, your manager presents your team's work. She leaves out something important. Add it without making her look bad.
say: And Raj's team finished the monitoring dashboards.
zh: 迭代评审会上，经理在介绍你们团队的工作，但漏了一个重要部分。补充一下，不要让她难堪。对方说：Raj 的团队完成了监控仪表板。
example: Thanks, Sarah. If I can add a bit there, we also set up alerts, so the on-call person gets a text if anything goes down.

task: At a busy steering meeting, the chair is about to finish early. You need to raise an important issue that isn't on the agenda. Ask for time.
say: If there's nothing else, we'll finish early today.
zh: 在一个议程很满的指导委员会会议上，主持人准备提前结束。你有一个不在议程上但很重要的问题要提。请求一点时间。对方说：如果没有别的事，我们今天就提前结束。
example: Sorry, there's one thing I'd like to raise before we finish. The security review found two issues that could delay go-live. Could I take five minutes on that?

task: A client keeps talking over you while you try to explain why their plan won't work. Stay calm, ask for a moment, and give the key fact.
say: No, no, we just move it all over the weekend and it'll be fine.
zh: 你想解释客户的计划为什么行不通，但客户一直抢话。保持冷静，请对方给你一点时间，然后说出关键事实。对方说：不不，我们周末全部搬过去就行了。
example: I hear you, and I'd love it to be that simple. Can I just explain one thing? There's about four terabytes of data, and copying it will take longer than a weekend.

task: Senior people are about to agree on something that goes against a decision made last month. Come in on the discussion and point this out.
say: So we're agreed: each team manages its own resource groups.
zh: 几位高层正准备达成一个与上个月决定相矛盾的共识。插话指出这一点。对方说：那就这么定了：每个团队管理自己的资源组。
example: Could I just come in on that? It sounds good, but it goes against what we decided last month about central control. Should we check that's okay first?
